name: Boolean-Prefix Cutset and Exact pc-Minor Transport
statement: For each distance-two pair $D=\{u,v\}$ of an ample family $H$, let $\mathcal I_D(H)$ be the Boolean interval of prefixes that contain every common neighbour of $u,v$ but neither endpoint. Then $H$ is nonpeelable exactly when $\bigcup_D\mathcal I_D(H)$ meets every maximal chain of $2^H$. This interval system transports exactly under pc-minors. Under restriction to a coordinate section $A$, an interval owned by $D\subseteq A$ becomes $\mathcal I_D(H)\cap2^A$. Under contraction $q:H\to\overline H$, pullback identifies $2^{\overline H}$ with the sublattice of unions of $q$-fibres, and each quotient interval pulls back to the interval from $q^{-1}C_{\overline H}(\overline u,\overline v)$ to $H\setminus q^{-1}\{\overline u,\overline v\}$ inside that sublattice.
proof: A total order corresponds to its maximal chain of prefixes. It fails at $D$ exactly when one prefix contains every common neighbour before either endpoint, which is exactly membership in $\mathcal I_D(H)$. The static distance-two elimination criterion proves the cutset equivalence. Restriction preserves the common-neighbour set of a retained distance-two pair, so intersecting the interval endpoints with $2^A$ gives the restriction formula. For contraction, inverse image is a lattice isomorphism from the quotient Boolean lattice to the fibre-saturated sublattice; applying it to each quotient interval gives the displayed pullback formula.
comments: The construction is finite, intrinsic, and order-free as a set system, but testing whether it meets every maximal chain remains equivalent to the forbidden ordering search.
